title: The loaf's arms
intro: You picked the loaf. Its body is settled and isn't under review here — only the arms move, so this is about one thing. The transition you flagged is fixed rather than offered as a choice: his arms used to jump straight to their new spot while his body eased down underneath them, which is what made the change of state read as a jump. They now ride the same springs his swinging arms already use, and the settle is heavier going under (620ms) than coming back (300ms, with a small overshoot). That's already in all three panes — watch the settle and the wake, not just where he ends up. "None of these" keeps the loaf exactly as you saw it.

steps.headline: Where should his arms end up once he's asleep?

variants.label: Tuck
variants.summary: Barely moved — his arms stay where you last saw them, just relaxed and dropped a little. The least he can do and still look asleep, and the least likely to be misread as a different creature. Also the least he DOES, so the settle is subtle.

variants.label: Dock
variants.summary: All the way down and pulled into his body, so his outline becomes one clean shape with nothing sticking out. Reads most deliberately as "put away" — and it's the one that stays legible when he's tiny or half-behind a window edge, because it's a silhouette rather than a set of parts.

variants.label: Flop
variants.summary: The wildcard: arms swung out flat to the sides, flumped. Funny rather than tidy, and the most characterful of the three — but it's also the most motion, and the widest, which is the one that could catch your eye when it shouldn't.

steps.headline: Should little z's drift up off him while he sleeps?
steps.changed: Whichever arms you pick, small z's can rise and fade above his head while he's under. (You skipped this last time — no problem, it's here again.)
steps.notice: It removes all doubt about what he's doing: nobody has to read his posture to know he's asleep. It's also the one part of this that isn't him — a bit of cartoon furniture floating on your desktop.
steps.risk: It never stops moving. A sleeping buddy is meant to be the quiet state, and that's exactly the ambient motion you said had to stay clearly below a real "needs attention" signal.
